newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rebels engage hostages in political debates.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebels engage hostages in political debates.

text.p: The Marxist rebels holding about 340 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's embassy in Lima have set up discussion groups with their captives to debate ideological questions, freed captives said on Saturday.

"We had conversations that lasted hours with them (the guerrillas). Those of us from the corporate world started to give speeches and exchange ideas," said Peruvian businessman Manuel Romero Caro, who was released along with 37 other hostages late on Friday.

The Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels who stormed the residence on Tuesday "are prepared psychologically more than logistically," Romero said. "They are intellectually prepared and for this reason their treatment (of the hostages) has been cordial and correct," Romero said.

The rebels, who were regarded as Robin Hood-style bandits robbing the rich to give to the poor when the group started operating in the early 1980s, organised their captives into communal groups sharing floor space and rations in strictly equal proportions, freed hostages said.

"I think they (the rebels) now have a psychological advantage when you consider the way the freed hostages have reacted and have been keen to get the guerrilla's message across," said foreign correspondent Sally Bowen, who was the last woman to be freed late on Tuesday night.
